function: Predicts excitation coefficients (beamforming vectors) maximizing directivity or array gain in a chosen direction for compact superdirective dipole arrays, from the radiated electric field (p. 3, p. 8).
system: 4-element printed dipole ULA and 4x4 UPA with mutual coupling, spacing 0.10-0.50 lambda (UPA 0.15-0.50), 1.6 GHz; no RIS; no communication link (p. 2, p. 8, p. 11).
method: MultiTransUNet-GAN: U-Net generator with Transformer and global spatial attention plus dense skip connections, CNN discriminator; supervised conditional GAN with NMSE loss, trained offline (p. 4-6).
data_channel: CST full-wave simulated radiated electric fields (2664 directions, 5-degree sampling) of 401 ULA spacings; labels from eigen-decomposition Eq. (6); 1,068,264 pairs, 70% training, 30% testing (p. 8).
test_conditions: 70/30 split of the 1,068,264 pairs (split unit not stated); unseen spacings claimed (p. 9) but no separate held-out-spacing test; gain and 4x4 UPA models trained separately (p. 8-11).
baselines: Non-learned: array theory-based [9], circuit theory-based [10], coupling matrix-based [2] methods; learned: TransUNet [23] (MultiTransUNet is the paper's own ablation) (p. 8, p. 9).
metrics: NMSE of excitation coefficients (dB), prediction accuracy Acc (%), directivity and array gain against theory and baselines, FLOPs, parameters (p. 8, p. 9).
complexity: Generator complexity O(Wm Hm Cm^2) multiplications; MultiTransUNet-GAN has 2046.54 M FLOPs and 18.99 M parameters (p. 7, p. 9).
q1_support: p. 8: "the CST software is employed to randomly model antenna arrays with various antenna spacing". The data are full-wave radiated fields of the authors' own dipole array; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 8: "split the datasets, using 70% for training and 30% for testing" (held-out part of the same data). p. 9: "encompassing the antenna spacings that have not been previously trained" is a claimed capability only; no experiment holds out spacings, and the Table III spacings 0.15-0.40 lambda lie inside the training range of 0.10-0.50 lambda.
q3_support: p. 8: "the array theory-based method [9], circuit theory-based method [10]" and the coupling matrix-based method [2] are compared on directivity (Table III, p. 9). p. 8: "the prediction performances of three models are compared: the original TransUNet model, the proposed MultiTransUNet model, and our proposed MultiTransUNet-GAN model" on accuracy.
q4_support: p. 7: "we evaluate the complexity of the proposed MultiTransUNet-GAN model in terms of the number of multiplications"; p. 9: "Table IV summarizes the FLOPs and the number of parameters of network models", with about 2046.54 M FLOPs for MultiTransUNet-GAN.
q5_support: p. 8: "the CST software is employed to randomly model antenna arrays with various antenna spacing". Data come from the authors' own simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Borderline on function: the learned model outputs beamforming weights (excitation coefficients) of a fixed compact array, not antenna hardware geometry, so it is kept as area 3; the paper models no communication link and reports directivity and gain, not rate. q3 counts TransUNet [23], an earlier published architecture applied to the same task; the MultiTransUNet variant is an ablation and is not counted.
